lyrics:
[Intro: chiming guitar, organ pad, steady kick]

[Verse 1: nostalgic male baritone]
Found a shoebox in the attic under thirty years of dust
Your handwriting on the label, little hearts for dots
Side A says "slow ones," Side B says "for driving"
I ain't owned a tape deck since the nineties

[Pre-Chorus: drums build]
Bought one at a yard sale for a dollar and a half
Pushed play and the ribbon came out like a laugh

[Chorus: big, open, singalong]
So I put a pencil in the cassette
Wound us back to seventeen
Your bare feet on the dashboard
My whole life in a tank of gasoline
Funny what a little plastic wheel can do
Pencil in the cassette, and I'm back with you
(Whoa-oh, whoa-oh, back with you)

[Verse 2: baritone, band rolling]
You taped it off the radio, the DJ's talking through
The first eight seconds of every song. I loved that about you.
There's a dog bark in the background, your mama calling "phone"
Three minutes of July that I get to take home

[Chorus: big, open, singalong]
So I put a pencil in the cassette
Wound us back to seventeen
Your bare feet on the dashboard
My whole life in a tank of gasoline
Funny what a little plastic wheel can do
Pencil in the cassette, and I'm back with you
(Whoa-oh, whoa-oh, back with you)

[Bridge: half-time, organ and voice]
I don't know where you landed. I hope it's somewhere kind.
I hope somebody keeps your songs in order, like you'd like.

[Final Chorus: full band, crowd on the chant]
So I put a pencil in the cassette
Wound us back to seventeen
Your bare feet on the dashboard
My whole life in a tank of gasoline
Funny what a little plastic wheel can do
Pencil in the cassette, and I'm back with you
(Whoa-oh, whoa-oh, back with you)

[Outro: tape hiss, a click, the deck stops]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 104 BPM, 4/4, D major. Steady, open and bittersweet, like driving at dusk.

VOICE: Male baritone, a little rough, fond and unhurried. He lifts into a stronger voice for the chorus. A crowd joins the wordless chant after each chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: Chiming electric guitar with a little delay, Hammond organ, strummed acoustic guitar, steady four-on-the-floor kick with a simple snare, bass, glockenspiel doubling the guitar in the chorus, tape hiss and a deck click at the end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and organ. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:42 Pre-chorus. 0:52 Chorus 1 and chant. 1:26 Verse 2. 1:54 Chorus 2 and chant. 2:28 Bridge, half-time. 2:48 Final chorus. 3:22 Outro, tape hiss, the click at 3:36.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2010s country with a 1980s heartland-rock frame: wide, warm, reverb on the snare, organ glowing.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first crowd chant at 1:14.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original remembers a summer through a singer. This one holds the actual object: her handwriting, her mother's voice in the background, a ribbon he has to repair by hand.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Finding, rewinding, back there, letting her go kindly.
